title: Trails and Glades
statementMd:
Vasya went for a walk in the park. The park has $*n*$ glades, numbered from 1 to $*n*$. There are $*m*$ trails between the glades. The trails are numbered from 1 to $*m*$, where the $*i*$-th trail connects glades $*x*_{*i*}$ and $*y*_{*i*}$. The numbers of the connected glades may be the same $(*x*_{*i*} = *y*_{*i*})$, which means that a trail connects a glade to itself. Also, two glades may have several non-intersecting trails between them.

Vasya is on glade 1, he wants to walk on all trails of the park exactly once, so that he can eventually return to glade 1. Unfortunately, Vasya does not know whether this walk is possible or not. Help Vasya, determine whether the walk is possible or not. If such walk is impossible, find the minimum number of trails the authorities need to add to the park in order to make the described walk possible.

Vasya can shift from one trail to another one only on glades. He can move on the trails in both directions. If Vasya started going on the trail that connects glades $*a*$ and $*b*$, from glade $*a*$, then he must finish this trail on glade $*b*$.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $*n*$ and $*m*$ $(1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{6}; 0 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{6})$ — the number of glades in the park and the number of trails in the park, respectively. Next $*m*$ lines specify the trails. The $*i*$-th line specifies the $*i*$-th trail as two space-separated numbers, $*x*_{*i*}$, $*y*_{*i*}$ $(1 ≤ *x*_{*i*}, *y*_{*i*} ≤ *n*)$ — the numbers of the glades connected by this trail.

## Output

Print the single integer — the answer to the problem. If Vasya's walk is possible without adding extra trails, print `0`, otherwise print the minimum number of trails the authorities need to add to the park in order to make Vasya's walk possible.

## Note

In the first test case the described walk is possible without building extra trails. For example, let's first go on the first trail, then on the second one, and finally on the third one.

In the second test case the described walk is impossible without adding extra trails. To make the walk possible, it is enough to add one trail, for example, between glades number one and two.
statementZhMd:
Vasya 去公园散步。公园中有 $*n*$ 个空地，编号从 1 到 $*n*$。空地之间有 $*m*$ 条小径。小径编号从 1 到 $*m*$，其中第 $*i*$ 条小径连接空地 $*x*_{*i*}$ 和 $*y*_{*i*}$。相连空地的编号可能相同 $(*x*_{*i*} = *y*_{*i*})$，这表示一条小径连接某个空地自身。此外，两个空地之间可能有多条互不相交的小径。

Vasya 位于空地 1，他想恰好经过公园中的每条小径一次，并最终回到空地 1。不幸的是，Vasya 不知道这样的行走是否可行。请帮助 Vasya 判断是否可行。如果不可行，请求出为了使上述行走成为可能，管理部门至少需要在公园中增建多少条小径。

Vasya 只能在空地处从一条小径转移到另一条小径。他可以沿小径的任意方向行走。如果 Vasya 从空地 $*a*$ 出发，开始走连接空地 $*a*$ 和 $*b*$ 的小径，那么他必须在空地 $*b*$ 结束这条小径。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*m*$ $(1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{6}; 0 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{6})$，分别表示公园中空地的数量和小径的数量。接下来 $*m*$ 行描述这些小径。第 $*i*$ 行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 $*x*_{*i*}$、$*y*_{*i*}$ $(1 ≤ *x*_{*i*}, *y*_{*i*} ≤ *n*)$，表示第 $*i*$ 条小径所连接的两个空地的编号。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数，即题目的答案。如果 Vasya 无需增建小径即可完成上述行走，则输出 `0`；否则输出为了使上述行走成为可能，管理部门至少需要增建的小径数量。

## 说明

在第一个测试用例中，无需增建小径即可完成上述行走。例如，可以先走第一条小径，然后走第二条小径，最后走第三条小径。

在第二个测试用例中，不增建小径无法完成上述行走。只需增建一条小径即可使行走成为可能，例如在编号为 1 和 2 的空地之间增建一条小径。
